key_insight: Finite relaxation times regularize the minimal magnetized spin-hydrodynamic model, replacing problematic first-order behavior with asymptotically linear propagation and finite relaxation poles.
engineering_relevance: The formulation offers a framework for computational models of relativistic magnetized fluids with spin, while characteristic speeds provide necessary light-cone checks.
method: Use an Israel–Stewart entropy current to derive transient stress and spin-flux equations.
Separate transport into longitudinal, transverse, and mixed channels under magnetic-field-induced anisotropy.
Analyze a minimal linear closure using infrared coefficient equations and ultraviolet characteristic expansions.
evidence_signal: For baseline parameters, the finite-relaxation model showed no growing modes on the sampled grid, unlike the unstable boost-sector poles and superlinear branches of the first-order truncation.
watch_item: The minimal closure omits explicit spin–magnetization coupling, and sampled stability plus characteristic-speed checks do not establish general stability or strong hyperbolicity.
paper_title: Anisotropic spin hydrodynamics in a magnetized medium: entropy-current formulation and minimal linear modes
